clue.text: The most daring items of underwear

parts.note: a bra is one item of women's underwear
a vest is another item of underwear, the British word for an undershirt

explanation.surface: Someone asks which pieces of lingerie are the boldest.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: two items of underwear, BRA and VEST, side by side. VEST is the British word for an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery is daring, so the superlative of brave describes whoever shows the greatest courage.

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim an obstinate dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clip' looks like a verb (trim the dog), but it is a noun: a strong spring-loaded clip for holding papers is named after this dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldog clip is a sprung stationery clamp, and the breed itself is famed for tenacious obstinacy.

indicators.note: a broken piece of jewellery is in bits, so its letters are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grows crosser after a piece of jewellery snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the letters of 'earring'; 'over' is a link meaning 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, which is a plain synonym of enraged.

clue.text: Guard loses his head at the gate

indicators.note: the guard losing his head means the opening letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier posted on guard

explanation.surface: A sentry at the gates is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' takes the first letter S off SENTRY; 'at the' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a way in, and an entry is likewise a means of entrance.

parts.note: a sexual attacker is a rapist

explanation.surface: An accusation that a physician is a sexual predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a verb or a title for the man accused, but it is the definition; the rest is simply split as THE plus RAPIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist is a practitioner who treats patients, a kind of healer loosely called a doctor.

parts.note: un is the French word for 'a', French being a continental language
a quilt is a bed cover

explanation.surface: A request to show off a duvet, which Britons once called a continental quilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'continental quilt' was the old British name for a duvet, but here 'a continental' gives UN, French for 'a', and 'quilt' gives COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to expose it by removing whatever conceals it.

parts.note: reads as a non-member of a trade union, but the union is marriage: someone not a partner in a wedded union

explanation.surface: A worker who has not joined the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a non-unionised worker; the union meant is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not part of a marriage is single, never having taken matrimonial vows.

explanation.surface: A description of features, perhaps a jawline, that look sculpted.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiselled features are clean-cut and sharply defined, and wood or stone cut with a chisel has been sculpted.

indicators.note: something overturned is tipped upside down, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Clive tipped a bus over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' rearranges CLIVE and HE together; 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is one example of a motor conveyance carrying passengers on roads.

clue.text: Foolish grin allowed to appear under the curl

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece appearing under another is placed after it
a foolish grin is daft, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: let means allowed, as in 'let him go'

explanation.surface: A silly smile is permitted to show beneath a lock of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolish' rearranges GRIN as RING; 'to appear under' puts LET below it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiralling lock of hair.

parts.note: reads as a man called Will leaving something, but the will is a testament bequeathing property to a beneficiary

explanation.surface: A man named Will abandons a task to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name; it is a legal will, which leaves an inheritance to its beneficiary.
explanation.definitionFit: A legatee is the person named in a testament to receive a bequest.

clue.text: What boxers do at the entrance, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an entrance is a way in

explanation.surface: Boxers' customary behaviour as they arrive at the arena door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' says the entrance, a WAY IN, sounds like the boxers' WEIGH-IN; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a bout, boxers stand on scales to confirm they are within their weight class.

clue.text: Mary and I did a turn for the farm-worker

indicators.note: doing a turn means turning around, so the letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people performed an act together for a labourer on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges MARY and I DID A together; 'and' joins the two parts of the fodder and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid is a woman employed to milk cows and make butter on a farm.

clue.text: Forty of the Romans pronouncedly do better

indicators.note: pronouncedly means the numeral is read out loud as letter names

parts.note: in Roman numerals forty is written XL

explanation.surface: An odd remark about forty Romans emphatically outperforming.
explanation.walkthrough: XL, the Roman numeral for forty, said as letter names ('ex-el') sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to surpass others or perform outstandingly well.

clue.text: American soldier right with the endless distance round

parts.note: GI is the usual term for an American private soldier

indicators.note: endless means the closing letter of the word 'the' is lopped off

explanation.surface: A US soldier is accompanied by the right and an unending journey around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the last letter of 'the', leaving TH; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A girth is the measurement around the middle of a body or object, its circumference.

clue.text: Passes on a tradition with utter ease

explanation.surface: Something inherited effortlessly through the generations.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders hand down customs to successors, and winning hands down is winning without any effort.

explanation.surface: A description of a brilliant brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of reasoning is the mind itself, and a person of formidable brainpower is also called this.

parts.note: a task is a job of work
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A committee is described as having work set for an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working party' reads as a committee; 's is a link ('is'). CE, for civil engineer, is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskforce is a group assembled to carry out a specific operation or piece of work.

clue.text: Has a commanding influence over Maidstone

indicators.note: over suggests the word is turned over, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Maidstone, the county town of Kent in England, is used purely for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone holds sway over a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidstone is the county town of Kent; 'over' looks like part of the definition but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to exercise control or authority over others.

parts.note: something lifeless is dead
a set is a group of things that belong together

explanation.surface: A corpse-like gang launches an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dead set' is a determined assault, as in 'make a dead set at someone'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead set is a concerted, resolute onslaught against someone or something.

clue.text: Exploit the chap, one regularly on a round

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An instruction to take advantage of a fellow who makes daily deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link here, giving no letters. In Britain a milkman delivers bottles door to door on a daily round.
explanation.definitionFit: A milkman follows the same delivery route to households every morning.

parts.note: a buzzer is a bee, and the male bee of a hive does none of the labour, leaving that to the workers

explanation.surface: A doorbell that is broken and never sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' suggests an electric bell; it is a bee, the idle male of the hive.
explanation.definitionFit: Male honeybees exist only to mate with the queen and gather no nectar, hence an idler is called one.

explanation.surface: A remark that a prayer book may be the second one.
explanation.definitionFit: Second, third and fourth are numbers giving position, and the book setting out the ceremony of ordaining clergy shares the name.

parts.note: an ear is a member, or organ, of the body

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of 'sent' have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave matter of a member being dismissed from the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SENT as NEST; 'having' is a link. 'member' reads as a club member but is a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and intensely serious in manner.

indicators.note: resort means sort again, so the letters are shuffled anew

explanation.surface: Climbing mountains is what someone does when all else fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as part of 'last resort' but means re-sort, rearranging A LAST; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlas range runs across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia in north-west Africa.

parts.note: to blow is to puff
a summer is one who sums, an adder of figures

explanation.surface: A snake in the heat of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who does sums: an ADDER. 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The puff adder is a venomous African viper that inflates itself when threatened.

clue.text: The said bunch of some old verses

indicators.note: said tells us the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: Someone quotes a collection of ancient poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' makes POSY, a bunch of flowers, sound like the answer; 'The' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Poesy is an archaic word for poetry or a body of verse.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone complains bitterly about blocked nasal passages.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'unpleasANT RAnting'; 'about' looks like a link but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity, especially one of the sinuses within bone.

explanation.surface: A remark that any ordinary person might turn out to be famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means any person at all, and a someone is also a person of importance or fame.

explanation.surface: A heading announcing the next railway service.
explanation.definitionFit: A dignitary's entourage follows them, and a train is likewise a line of attendants.

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word 'The' is removed

parts.note: Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cruel young woman has somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle letter H out of 'The', leaving TE; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the right to occupy rented premises, and so a home held on lease.

clue.text: Man in the starting place back on the shoulder

indicators.note: in says the man is put inside the other piece
back means the golfing word is read from end to start

parts.note: in golf the tee is where each hole starts
Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man stands at the start line with his back to someone's shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TEE into EET, and 'in' puts PAUL inside it after the first E. The definition describes the answer by where it is worn.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulet is an ornamental strap or fringed pad worn on the top of a uniform jacket at each side.
